title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath and follow-up.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 77-year-old female who presented with sudden onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain. Imaging confirmed an acute pulmonary embolism. Patient was started on anticoagulation therapy.

[Update] The patient returns today for a follow-up regarding her acute pulmonary embolism diagnosed two weeks ago via CT imaging. She reports that her breathing has significantly improved since starting her medication. She denies any new chest pain or increased shortness of breath. She states she has been compliant with her anticoagulation regimen and denies any unusual bleeding or bruising.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Respiratory: Positive (improved shortness of breath)
Cardiovascular: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Negative
Neurological: Negative

Medication List:
Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezing or crackles.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs.

Assessment:
1. Acute pulmonary embolism. Patient is in the first months of anticoagulant treatment.

Plan:
Continue current dose of Rivaroxaban. Follow up in 4 weeks for continued monitoring of respiratory status.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, PA-C
October 14, 2026
explanations: Acute pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale, under initial treatment: I26.99 (HCC 267).

distractors.why: The embolism is acute and still being treated.
The embolism is documented as acute.
